consigna.es: Escucha y elige quién es Sara.

items.audio: This is my mother. Her name is Sara. My sister is ten.

feedback.es: Dice This is my mother. Her name is Sara: Sara es su madre. Ten es la edad de su hermana.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige dónde está la bolsa.

items.audio: There are two books on the table. The bag is under the chair.

feedback.es: Dice The bag is under the chair: la bolsa está debajo de la silla.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige lo que la persona nunca hace.

items.audio: I always eat breakfast at home, but I never eat dinner at school.

feedback.es: Never significa nunca: nunca cena en la escuela.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige lo que la persona pide.

items.audio: Can I have a tea and a sandwich, please? No juice, thanks.

feedback.es: Pide a tea and a sandwich y dice No juice: no quiere jugo.

consigna.es: Lee y elige cuántos años tiene la hermana de Ana.

items.texto: Hello! I am Ana. I am ten. I have got one brother and one sister. My brother Leo is eight. My sister is three.

feedback.es: El texto dice My sister is three. Ten es la edad de Ana y eight la de Leo.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué hay junto a la cocina.

items.texto: Welcome to my house! There is a big kitchen. There are two bedrooms. The bathroom is next to the kitchen. The sofa is in the room.

feedback.es: El mensaje dice The bathroom is next to the kitchen: el baño está junto a la cocina.

consigna.es: Lee y elige qué hace Leo a veces.

items.texto: Leo usually gets up at six. He always eats breakfast and then he goes to school. He sometimes studies English at night. He never works on Monday.

feedback.es: Sometimes significa a veces: a veces estudia inglés por la noche.

consigna.es: Lee la respuesta de Sam y elige por qué no puede el viernes.

items.texto: Hi Ana! I'd love to meet you, but I can't on Friday because I am working at home. I am at school on Monday, but I am free on Saturday.

feedback.es: Sam dice que no puede el viernes because I am working at home: porque está trabajando en casa.

consigna.es: Completa con la forma correcta de be.

items.texto: My parents ___ at home.

feedback.es: Parents es plural, así que se usa are.

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre Mia.

items.texto: Mia ___ milk at breakfast.

feedback.es: Con he/she/it el verbo lleva -s en presente simple: drinks.

consigna.es: Completa con el pronombre que reemplaza a Ana.

items.texto: Ana is my friend. I like ___.

feedback.es: Después del verbo like se usa el pronombre objeto her.

consigna.es: Completa con lo que pasa ahora mismo.

items.texto: Sam ___ a book now.

feedback.es: Now indica una acción en este momento: presente continuo is reading.

consigna.es: Completa con la palabra de la familia.

items.texto: Your mother's brother is your ___.

feedback.es: El hermano de tu madre es tu tío: uncle. Aunt es tía y cousin es primo.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que encaja en el contexto.

items.texto: We eat dinner at the ___ in the kitchen.

feedback.es: En la cocina se cena en la mesa: at the table.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la rutina.

items.texto: I get up at seven in the ___.

feedback.es: A las siete de levantarse es por la mañana: in the morning.

consigna.es: Completa el pedido en el restaurante.

items.texto: I don't eat meat. I'd like a salad ___ chicken.

feedback.es: Sin carne significa sin pollo: without.

consigna.es: Describe tu cuarto en dos frases: There is… y There are…, con un lugar.

items.respuesta: There is a bed in my room. There are two chairs next to the table.
aceptadas: There is a sofa in the room. There are three books on the table.
There is a bed in my room and there are two chairs on the floor.

feedback.es: Usa There is con un solo elemento, There are con varios, y un lugar como in o on.

consigna.es: Escribe dos frases sobre tu rutina: a qué hora te levantas y qué haces después.

items.respuesta: I get up at seven o'clock. I go to school at eight.
aceptadas: I get up at six. I eat breakfast and I study English.
I get up at eight o'clock and I work at home.

feedback.es: Incluye I get up con una hora usando at, y otra acción de tu día.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige cómo viaja al trabajo esta semana.

items.audio: Normally I cycle, but my bicycle is broken this week. I hate walking, so I'm taking the bus.
opciones: On foot, because it is healthy.
By bicycle, as in a normal week.
By bus, because of a broken bicycle.

feedback.es: Normalmente va en bicicleta, pero esta semana su bicicleta está rota y no le gusta caminar, así que toma el autobús.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige por qué no compró pan.

items.audio: Yesterday I didn't buy any bread. I had enough money, but the shop was closed.

feedback.es: Dice que tenía dinero suficiente; no compró pan porque la tienda estaba cerrada.

consigna.es: Escucha el aviso y elige qué está prohibido.

items.audio: Visitors must wear a helmet here. You mustn't touch the machines, and you should ask a colleague for help.

feedback.es: «Mustn't» expresa prohibición: no se pueden tocar las máquinas. El casco es obligatorio («must») y pedir ayuda es solo un consejo («should»).

consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige qué pide la persona.

items.audio: Hello, the shower in my flat doesn't work. Could you send someone to repair it today, please?
opciones: A repair visit on the same day.
A new shower for the flat.
Someone to repair it next week.

feedback.es: Pide que alguien vaya hoy a arreglar la ducha; no pide una ducha nueva ni que lo hagan otro día.

consigna.es: Lee el perfil y elige por qué Eva está en la oficina esta semana.

items.texto: I'm Eva. My hours are flexible, but my deadlines are fixed. I rarely go to the office: my team usually meets online. This week, however, I'm working at the office because we have a big project.
opciones: Her working hours are now fixed.
There is important work to finish.
The online system is not working.

feedback.es: Eva dice que esta semana, excepcionalmente, va a la oficina porque hay un proyecto grande. Sus horarios son flexibles; lo fijo son los plazos.

consigna.es: Lee la historia y elige por qué Leo no fue a la fiesta.

items.texto: Last Saturday Leo wanted to go to Mia's party. In the afternoon he took his bicycle to the park, but he fell and hurt his foot. He didn't go to the party. He stayed at home and watched a film with his brother.
opciones: He preferred a film with his brother.
His bicycle was broken after the fall.
He hurt his foot in a fall.

feedback.es: Leo quería ir, pero se cayó de la bicicleta y se lastimó el pie; por eso se quedó en casa. La película fue su plan alternativo, no el motivo.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué ha hecho ya Sam.

items.texto: Hi Nora! I've already booked the hotel for our trip. It's cheaper than the other hotels, and it's near the station. But I haven't bought the tickets yet. Can you look at the prices today? Thanks, Sam
opciones: He has checked the ticket prices.
He has bought the train tickets.
He has reserved a hotel room.

feedback.es: Sam escribe que ya ha reservado el hotel. Los precios y los boletos siguen pendientes: le pide a Nora que mire los precios hoy.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige cuál es la solución que propone Paula.

items.texto: Hi Jon, thanks for the invitation! I'd love to come to your party, but I can't on Friday. I have to work late. How about Saturday afternoon instead? I can bring some fruit and a cake. Please answer soon!
opciones: Move the party to Saturday afternoon.
Come late to the party on Friday.

feedback.es: Paula no puede el viernes y propone el sábado por la tarde. No habla de llegar tarde ni de salir antes del trabajo.

consigna.es: Elige la opción correcta para completar la frase.

items.texto: Right now Ben ___ a bigger flat, so he is looking at new places.

feedback.es: «Want» es un verbo de estado y no se usa en continuo, aunque sea «ahora»; con Ben lleva -s.

consigna.es: Elige la opción correcta para completar la pregunta.

items.texto: Did you ___ the match last night?

feedback.es: Con «did» el verbo va en forma base: el pasado ya lo marca «did».

consigna.es: Completa la pregunta con el participio correcto.

items.texto: Have you ever ___ pizza?

feedback.es: «Have you ever...?» pide el participio pasado: eaten.

consigna.es: Completa el aviso del museo con la opción correcta.

items.texto: You ___ pay to enter the museum on Sundays. It's free.

feedback.es: Sin obligación se usa «don't have to»: la entrada es gratis, no hace falta pagar. «Mustn't» sería una prohibición.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase.

items.texto: My ___ is long: I take two buses and a train to get to the office every morning.

feedback.es: «Commute» es el trayecto diario al trabajo; «shift» es el turno y «deadline» el plazo.

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo que mejor completa el texto.

items.texto: The train is more ___ than the bus. The bus is often late, but the train always arrives on time.

feedback.es: «Reliable» es fiable: se puede confiar en que llegue a la hora. El texto no habla de comodidad, gente ni precio.

consigna.es: Completa lo que dice el médico con la palabra correcta.

items.texto: A cough and a fever are common ___ of a cold.

feedback.es: «Symptoms» son los síntomas: señales de una enfermedad, como la tos y la fiebre.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que completa el mensaje.

items.texto: My tablet is frozen. I have to ___ it: I turn it off and then turn it on again.

feedback.es: «Restart» es reiniciar: apagar y volver a encender. «Charge» es cargar la batería y «connect», conectarse.

consigna.es: Escribe 2 frases en pasado: algo que hiciste ayer y algo que no hiciste.

items.respuesta: Yesterday I went to work. I didn't cook dinner at home.
aceptadas: Yesterday I visited my friend. I didn't watch television.
I studied English in the morning. I did not go to the gym.
We played football after work. We didn't call our friends.

feedback.es: Usa el pasado simple: una acción afirmativa y una negativa con «didn't» + verbo en forma base.

consigna.es: Escribe 2 frases con «going to»: un plan tuyo y otro de alguien más.

items.respuesta: This weekend I'm going to visit my cousin. My parents are going to cook lunch.
aceptadas: On Saturday I am going to watch a film. My friend is going to bring some snacks.
I'm going to study English tomorrow. We're going to play football on Sunday.

feedback.es: «Going to» expresa planes: sujeto + am/is/are + going to + verbo. Escribe uno tuyo y otro de otra persona.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué hacía la persona cuando empezó a llover.

items.audio: I was repairing my bike when it started to rain, so I took it inside.

feedback.es: Dice «I was repairing my bike when it started to rain»: estaba arreglando la bicicleta cuando la lluvia la interrumpió.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué harán si el tren se retrasa.

items.audio: If the train is delayed, we will call the hotel and ask for a later check-in.
opciones: They will take a taxi home
They will phone the place where they will stay

feedback.es: La condición es «if the train is delayed, we will call the hotel»: llamarán al hotel.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige por qué Leo no recoge el paquete hoy.

items.audio: Mia told Leo that the shop was closed, so he is going to get the parcel on Monday.
opciones: He is busy at work today
The store is not open today

feedback.es: Mia le dijo a Leo que la tienda estaba cerrada, así que irá el lunes.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué condición pone la persona para prestar el coche.

items.audio: You can borrow my car, but only if you bring it back before nine. If not, I will need a taxi.
opciones: Return it at a fixed time

feedback.es: Dice «only if you bring it back before nine»: solo lo presta si lo devuelves antes de las nueve.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige lo que Sam aún no ha hecho.

items.texto: Hi Lena, I have already repaired the broken lamp, so it works now. I have not checked the heater yet. I am going to look at it on Friday, and I will send you a message when it is ready. Thanks, Sam
opciones: He has not looked at the heater
He has not fixed the lamp
He has not sent any message

feedback.es: Sam escribe «I have not checked the heater yet»: la lámpara ya está reparada, pero la calefacción todavía no la ha revisado.

consigna.es: Lee el anuncio y elige qué pasa con cada aparato antes de repararlo.

items.texto: Do you need someone who can fix your computer? Our team helps people with broken screens and slow systems. Every device is checked before repair, and you receive a confirmation by email. We are open from Monday to Saturday.
opciones: The owner must pay a deposit

feedback.es: El anuncio dice «Every device is checked before repair»: primero se revisa.

consigna.es: Lee el correo y elige qué pide el viajero.

items.texto: I am writing about my ferry journey on Monday. The ferry was delayed for three hours, and I am still waiting for an answer. I have the receipt and the booking code. I would like a refund, because I missed my appointment.
opciones: A phone call from the port

feedback.es: Escribe «I would like a refund»: pide que le devuelvan el dinero.

consigna.es: Lee la ficha del proyecto y elige quién se encarga de la seguridad.

items.texto: The brief says the goal is to make a quiet garden behind the library. The audience is families with young children. The budget is £600, so the team must not spend more. Volunteers will clean the garden on Saturday, and the council is responsible for the safety plan.

feedback.es: La ficha dice que el ayuntamiento es responsable del plan de seguridad.

consigna.es: Completa con la forma verbal correcta.

items.texto: We were late because the bus ___ before we got to the stop.

feedback.es: La causa ocurrió antes de llegar a la parada, por eso se usa el pasado perfecto: «had left».

consigna.es: Completa esta situación imaginaria.

items.texto: If I ___ more time, I would learn another language.

feedback.es: Una situación irreal y poco probable usa «if» + pasado y «would» en el resultado: «had».

consigna.es: Completa este proceso con la forma correcta.

items.texto: In this bakery, the bread ___ every morning before seven.

feedback.es: El pan recibe la acción, no la realiza: se usa la pasiva, «is made».

consigna.es: Completa con la expresión que marca la condición.

items.texto: The club can use the hall ___ it pays £40 a week.

feedback.es: «Only if» indica que el club puede usar el salón solo con esa condición; «unless» expresaría lo contrario.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que significa «al final».

items.texto: We waited for two hours, and ___ the bus arrived.

feedback.es: «Eventually» indica que algo ocurre al final, después de un tiempo de espera.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión con dos palabras que cabe en la frase.

items.texto: Reception called, so I went to ___ my parcel.

feedback.es: «Pick up» significa recoger algo que está esperando; «turn off» y «fill in» no encajan.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que forma la combinación natural.

items.texto: We must ___ the deadline on Friday.

feedback.es: «Meet a deadline» es la combinación natural para cumplir un plazo.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que describe esta información.

items.texto: The report says the road may close, but this is not confirmed. So the information is ___.

feedback.es: El informe dice que el cierre no está confirmado, por eso la información es «uncertain».

consigna.es: Escribe qué harás tú si mañana llueve, en 1 o 2 frases.

items.respuesta: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay at home and read a book.
aceptadas: If it rains tomorrow, I will stay home and watch a film.
If the weather is bad, I will stay at home and cook dinner.
evidenciasEscritura: if the weather is not good

feedback.es: Una condición probable usa «if» + presente y «will» en el resultado.

consigna.es: Da un consejo a un amigo cansado con «If I were you...», en 1 frase.

items.respuesta: If I were you, I would sleep earlier and avoid coffee at night.
aceptadas: If I were you, I would take a break and sleep more.
If I was you, I would go to bed earlier.
evidenciasEscritura: if i were in your position
if i were in your place

feedback.es: Un consejo imaginario usa «If I were you, I would...» y una acción concreta.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué descubre la persona sobre Mia.

items.audio: I called Mia at nine, but she didn't answer. Her brother told me she had already left for work by then, so I sent her a message.
opciones: Mia had gone out before the call.
Mia was still at home when the call came.
Mia left home right after the call.

feedback.es: «Had already left… by then»: Mia ya se había ido antes de la llamada de las nueve.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué piensa la persona sobre los vecinos.

items.audio: Their car is still outside, so they can't have gone far. They may have walked to the shop around the corner.
opciones: They have probably travelled a long way.
They are certainly inside the house.
They are probably not far from home.

feedback.es: «Can't have gone far» y «may have walked» deducen que están cerca, no lejos ni seguros en casa.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige quién revisará el calefactor.

items.audio: The heater stopped working yesterday. I'm having an engineer look at it tomorrow morning, and he will send me the bill afterwards.
opciones: The speaker will check it alone.
A professional will check it for the speaker.
The speaker will buy a new one tomorrow.

feedback.es: «I'm having an engineer look at it» (have + algo + verbo): la persona contrata a un técnico, no lo revisa ella.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué espera la persona dentro de un año.

items.audio: By the end of the year, I will have saved enough money to buy a small car. This time next year, I will be driving to work.
opciones: The speaker will still be saving up for a car.
The speaker will be looking for a new job nearby.
The speaker will be going to work in a car.

feedback.es: Con «will have saved» y «will be driving» anticipa que ya tendrá ahorros y un coche que usará para trabajar.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige qué encontraron al llegar al pueblo.

items.texto: Last Sunday we took Grandma to the village where she grew up. She had promised us the best bread in the country, but when we arrived, the bakery had become a café. The old school had closed years ago, too. Grandma laughed and said she would make the bread herself, as she had done when she was a girl.
opciones: The bakery was now used for something different.
The school had closed only a few days earlier.
Grandma's old house had been sold.

feedback.es: «The bakery had become a café»: el local ya no era panadería; la escuela llevaba años cerrada («years ago»).

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige qué todavía no ha ocurrido con el pan.

items.texto: In our village, bread is still made in the traditional way. The flour is brought from a farm nearby and mixed by hand. After that, the dough is left to rest for two hours, and then it is baked in a big oven. The bread has been sold in the local market for forty years, and it will soon be sent to other shops in the region.
opciones: It has been sold in the village market.
It is baked in a big oven.
It has reached other shops in the region.

feedback.es: «Will soon be sent» es futuro: aún no llega a otras tiendas. Lo otro ya ocurre o ya ocurrió («is baked», «has been sold»).

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige por qué Sam debe llamar antes de las seis.

items.texto: Hi Sam, Carla phoned at four. She asked whether you had booked the tickets, and I told her you were still waiting for an email. She said you should call her before six because she is leaving for the airport after that. Can you ring her, please? Dad
opciones: The tickets will stop being available at six.
Carla will be travelling after that time.
Dad will need to use the phone then.

feedback.es: Carla dijo que después de las seis sale hacia el aeropuerto, así que luego no podrá hablar con calma.

consigna.es: Lee la noticia y elige la frase que resume bien la situación.

items.texto: Local news: A fire started at the old workshop on Tuesday night. According to the police, nobody was hurt, although two streets were closed for hours. It seems that the fire was caused by an electrical problem, but this has not been confirmed. The workshop owner has not yet answered any questions.
opciones: The police say nobody was hurt, but the cause is unclear.
Everyone agrees that an electrical problem caused the fire last night.
The owner has told reporters there was no electrical problem at all.

feedback.es: Atribuido a la policía: nadie herido. La causa eléctrica es solo una sospecha («It seems… not been confirmed») y el dueño aún no habló.

consigna.es: Elige la forma verbal que completa la frase sobre el pasado.

items.texto: I didn't recognise him because he ___ a lot since our last meeting.

feedback.es: El cambio es anterior al momento pasado de «didn't recognise» y dura desde «since»: pide past perfect, «had changed».

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre un pasado imaginado.

items.texto: If I had known about the traffic, I ___ home earlier.

feedback.es: Para imaginar un resultado distinto en el pasado se usa if + past perfect y would have + participio.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra relativa que completa la frase.

items.texto: My neighbour, ___ dog is very noisy at night, is moving to another town.

feedback.es: «Whose» indica posesión: el perro del vecino. Who o which no pueden ir delante de «dog».

consigna.es: Elige la question tag correcta para cerrar la frase.

items.texto: You haven't seen my keys, ___?

feedback.es: La frase es negativa, así que la tag es afirmativa y repite el auxiliar: «have you?».

consigna.es: Elige el conector que completa el mensaje.

items.texto: The road was closed. ___, we arrived an hour late.

feedback.es: La segunda frase es consecuencia de la primera: «As a result» introduce el resultado.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que va con la frase deportiva.

items.texto: She trained for years and finally broke the school ___ in the 100 metres.

feedback.es: La combinación natural es «break a record»: superar la mejor marca existente.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase.

items.texto: Everyone trusts Nina because of her ___.

feedback.es: Después de «her» hace falta un sustantivo: «honesty» (de honest + -y); honest es adjetivo.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que matiza la noticia.

items.texto: ___, the concert has been cancelled, but I haven't seen an official announcement.

feedback.es: «Apparently» presenta algo que se oyó pero no está confirmado; las otras dos expresan certeza oficial o total.

consigna.es: Escribe 2 frases sobre algo que hacías de niño y algo que ya no haces.

items.respuesta: When I was a child, I used to play football with my cousins every afternoon. I don't play any more, but now I watch the matches on television.
aceptadas: As a kid, I used to walk to school with my brother. Today I go by bus because it is far from our house.

feedback.es: Usa «used to» para el hábito pasado y un contraste con el presente (now, today, I don't).

consigna.es: Escribe 2-3 frases: llegaste tarde y qué habría pasado si hubieras salido antes.

items.respuesta: Yesterday I was late for my appointment because I missed the bus. If I had left home earlier, I would have caught it. I would have arrived on time.
aceptadas: I was late to the meeting. If I had got up earlier, I wouldn't have missed the train. I would have arrived on time.

feedback.es: Combina if + past perfect con would have + participio para imaginar un pasado distinto.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué es verdad sobre quien habla.

items.audio: When I first moved here, the traffic kept me awake every night. Now I hardly notice it, but my sister, who is staying with me, can't sleep at all. She says she could never live with it.
opciones: The traffic no longer troubles the speaker.
The speaker still cannot sleep because of the traffic.
The speaker's sister has got used to the noise.

feedback.es: Al principio el ruido le quitaba el sueño, pero ahora casi no lo nota; quien no duerme es su hermana, no quien habla.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige cómo llegaron finalmente a la costa.

items.audio: We were going to drive to the coast, but the car broke down. A neighbour offered us his van, although it was too small for everyone. In the end, we took the train.
opciones: They all went in a neighbour's van.
They repaired the car and left later.

feedback.es: Iban a ir en auto, el vecino ofreció una camioneta demasiado pequeña y al final tomaron el tren: usaron transporte público.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué siente la persona sobre su decisión.

items.audio: If I had accepted the job in Madrid, I would be living there now. Sometimes I wonder about it. But if I had gone, I wouldn't have met my partner, so I have no regrets.
opciones: The speaker is content with the decision.
The speaker wishes to have moved to Madrid.
The speaker plans to move to Madrid soon.

feedback.es: Duda a veces, pero concluye que no se arrepiente: si hubiera aceptado el trabajo, no habría conocido a su pareja.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige cuál es la postura de la portavoz.

items.audio: The spokesperson admitted that the company had made a mistake, but insisted that nobody had been hurt. She promised to publish a full report, although critics claim the figures are exaggerated.
opciones: She denies that the company did anything wrong at all.
She admits some blame but denies any harm.
She refuses to give any more information to critics.

feedback.es: Admite un error pero insiste en que nadie salió herido: acepta parte de la culpa y niega el daño.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué opina la autora de lo que dice su compañera.

items.texto: Hi Lena, it's been ages! I've been living in Leeds since September and I still can't get used to the weather. Back home it never snowed, so I wasn't used to wearing three coats! Lately I've been cooking a lot because the food at the café is so expensive. My flatmate says I'll get used to it, but I'm not so sure. Honestly, I miss the sun. Write soon!
opciones: She believes her flatmate is probably right.
She is planning to leave Leeds soon.
She doubts what her flatmate says.

feedback.es: Su compañera dice que se acostumbrará, pero ella responde «I'm not so sure» y añade que extraña el sol: no está convencida.

consigna.es: Lee el correo y elige para qué lo escribe el cliente.

items.texto: Dear Mr Hill, On Monday I took my car to your garage because the brakes were making a strange noise. You promised to have it ready by Wednesday, but I only got it back on Friday, and the noise is still there. I'm not asking for a refund, but I would like your mechanic to look at it again, free of charge. I hope we can sort this out.
opciones: To ask the garage to look at the brakes again at no cost
To ask for a refund for the repair
To thank the garage for returning the car by Wednesday

feedback.es: Pide que revisen de nuevo el auto sin costo; aclara que no quiere un reembolso, y se queja de que el ruido sigue.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cómo se siente la autora al final.

items.texto: Last Friday I found a wallet with two hundred dollars inside. Money is a problem this month, and I could easily have kept it. But the owner's address was on his card, so I took the wallet to his door. He was so grateful that he insisted on buying me lunch. I'm glad I did the right thing. Still, I sometimes think about the laptop I could have bought.
opciones: She wishes she had kept the money.
She is satisfied, though not free from regret.
She is angry that the owner did not thank her.

feedback.es: Se alegra de haber hecho lo correcto, pero aún piensa en la laptop que pudo comprar: satisfacción con un pequeño pesar.

consigna.es: Lee el artículo y elige qué opina el autor del titular de un informe.

items.texto: A new study claims that teenagers who sleep less than six hours tend to get lower marks. The researchers, however, admit that their sample was small, and other things, such as diet or stress, may well be involved. Nevertheless, the headline in one report states that lack of sleep causes bad results, which is arguably exaggerated.
opciones: They describe the study's results fairly.
They say more than the study can really show.
They are too cautious about what the study found.

feedback.es: El autor dice que el titular es «arguably exaggerated»: afirma una causa que el estudio no puede demostrar.

consigna.es: Elige la forma que completa la frase.

items.texto: Night shifts are still hard for me, but I ___ sleeping in the daytime more and more.

feedback.es: «More and more» indica un proceso en curso: am getting used to + -ing. «Am used to» ya sería costumbre y «used to» no lleva -ing.

consigna.es: Elige la opción gramaticalmente correcta.

items.texto: My teacher made me ___ the whole essay again because of one small mistake.

feedback.es: Después de make + persona va el verbo sin to: made me write. Con get sí se usa to (got me to write).

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que completa la condición.

items.texto: Tom missed the last train last night. If he had caught it, he ___ at home now.

feedback.es: La condición es pasada, pero el resultado es de hoy (now): condicional mixto, had + participio en el if y would + verbo en la otra parte.

consigna.es: Elige el conector que completa la frase.

items.texto: You can borrow my laptop ___ you promise to look after it.

feedback.es: Provided that introduce una condición necesaria: te la presto si prometes cuidarla. Unless significaría lo contrario.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que encaja en la frase.

items.texto: Mia ran up all the stairs, so she arrived ___.

feedback.es: Out of breath es quedarse sin aliento por el esfuerzo; out of order es «averiado» y out of date, «desactualizado».

consigna.es: Elige el verbo compuesto que completa la frase.

items.texto: After their argument, Jo and Mia didn't speak for weeks, but last night they finally ___.

feedback.es: Make up es reconciliarse después de una pelea; fall out es pelearse y hit it off, llevarse bien desde el principio.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa el mensaje.

items.texto: It's a surprise party for Clara, so please don't ___ before Saturday!

feedback.es: Spill the beans es revelar un secreto sin querer; break the ice rompe el hielo y bite the bullet es aguantar algo difícil.

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo que describe ese artículo.

items.texto: The article gives only one side and ignores the critics, so it is clearly ___.

feedback.es: Biased es parcial: favorece a un solo lado. Balanced y accurate describirían un artículo que muestra ambas posturas o es exacto.

consigna.es: Explica por qué llegaste agotado anoche: llevabas varias horas haciendo algo.

items.respuesta: I was exhausted last night because I had been working in the garden for five hours.
aceptadas: When I got home I was out of breath, because I had been running for an hour and I had not eaten.

feedback.es: Had been + -ing cuenta la actividad que duraba antes de llegar agotado; for + duración indica cuánto, y because explica la causa.

consigna.es: Di cómo sería tu vida hoy si hubieras estudiado otra carrera y por qué no lo hiciste.

items.respuesta: If I had studied medicine, I would be a doctor now. However, I chose design because I have always loved drawing.
aceptadas: If I'd studied law, I would be living in another city now. I didn't choose it since I wanted to stay near my family.

feedback.es: Condicional mixto: if I had + participio para la decisión pasada y would be o would + verbo para el efecto actual; explica la razón con because.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué dice la hablante sobre su hermana.

items.audio: My sister will interrupt me every time I start a story. Yesterday she did it again, just when I reached the best part. It is so annoying.
opciones: Her sister is going to interrupt her tomorrow.
Her sister often does this, and she hates it.
Her sister did this only once, yesterday.

feedback.es: «Will» describe una costumbre típica (no un futuro); con «every time» y «so annoying» se ve que lo hace a menudo y le molesta.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué pasó con la prisa.

items.audio: We needn't have hurried. When we arrived, the hall was half empty, because the concert wasn't due to start for another hour. Next time, we'll leave later and have dinner first.
opciones: They arrived after the concert had started.
They took their time because they knew it was early.
They rushed, but there was no need to.

feedback.es: «Needn't have hurried» significa que corrieron y resultó innecesario: llegaron con una hora de sobra. No es lo mismo que no correr.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué se concluye sobre la leyenda del puente.

items.audio: It is said that the old bridge is haunted. The mayor denied that anything strange has ever happened there, and the historian admitted that nobody has any proof, although the legend is very old.
opciones: Both officials say the bridge is really haunted.
The legend is old, but there is no evidence for it.
The historian found proof, but the mayor denied it.

feedback.es: Se dice que está encantado, pero el alcalde lo niega y el historiador admite que nadie tiene pruebas: la leyenda es antigua y sin evidencia.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué opina la persona sobre los móviles y el sueño.

items.audio: Some teachers argue that phones help students learn, given that they can look up information quickly. However, the survey suggests that the more students use their phones at night, the less they sleep. That does not prove phones are the only cause.
opciones: Phones may harm sleep, but other causes are possible.
Phones are the only cause of students' sleep problems.
Phones do not affect sleep, because they help students learn.

feedback.es: Reconoce una posible relación con el sueño, pero aclara que no prueba que los móviles sean la única causa.

consigna.es: Lee la anécdota y elige por qué la autora dice «So there I am».

items.texto: Last Friday I was at the station when I noticed that my ticket was missing. So there I am, on the platform, checking every pocket, and the train is arriving. I sprint to the machine, grab a ticket and run back just as the whistle blows. The doors close behind me. Honestly, those thirty seconds felt like an hour, and my heart is still racing!
opciones: To say that she is still waiting at the station today
To make the scene feel as if it were happening now
To show that she often loses her ticket

feedback.es: El presente histórico («So there I am») acerca la escena al lector y la hace más vívida.

consigna.es: Lee la noticia y elige qué se sabe con seguridad.

items.texto: The mayor is said to have resigned last night, although the council has not confirmed the news. After reading the report on the old bridge, two neighbours claim that the repairs should have started years ago. The mayor's office denied that there was any danger. No sooner had the news arrived than shoppers began to ask whether the bridge would stay open. Nobody has said anything official yet.
opciones: The council has announced that the mayor resigned.
The mayor's office has accepted that the bridge is dangerous.
The news that the mayor resigned is not confirmed.

feedback.es: «Is said to have resigned» y «has not confirmed» indican un rumor sin confirmar; la oficina del alcalde, además, negó el peligro.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige cuál es el propósito principal de Mia.

items.texto: Hi Leo, I see your point about the cost, but I'm afraid the schedule is too tight. The party is due to start at six on Saturday, and the food is set to arrive at four. I will pay half on condition that you book the room. Could we postpone the party to 27 June instead? I'd appreciate it if you could let me know today. Thanks, Mia
opciones: To offer a compromise and suggest a new date
To reject Leo's idea and end the discussion
To ask Leo to pay everything to keep the party on Saturday

feedback.es: Mia reconoce el argumento de Leo, ofrece pagar la mitad con una condición y propone otra fecha: busca un punto medio.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la postura de la autora.

items.texto: Critics argue that closing the city centre to cars would hurt local shops. The evidence, however, points the other way: in towns that tried it, the number of shoppers rose by a third, given that more people walked. What worries traders is not the ban itself but the change. A few months later, most of them would not go back to the old way, and the sales figures keep rising.
opciones: She agrees that shops will lose many customers.
She thinks the ban is more likely to help shops than harm them.
She believes traders will never accept the ban.

feedback.es: Presenta la objeción («Critics argue») y la rebate con datos («points the other way»): los comercios ganan clientes.

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre el abuelo con la forma correcta.

items.texto: My grandfather is ninety, but every afternoon he ___ sit in the garden for hours, humming old songs.

feedback.es: «Will» expresa una conducta típica en el presente; «would» y «used to» hablan de hábitos del pasado.

consigna.es: Elige la forma que completa la frase enfática.

items.texto: Hardly ___ the band started when the power went out.

feedback.es: Tras «hardly» se invierte el auxiliar y se usa el pasado perfecto: «Hardly had… when…».

consigna.es: Elige la forma que une las dos acciones, hechas por los mismos estudiantes.

items.texto: ___ the exam, the students left the room quietly.

feedback.es: «Having + participio» presenta una acción terminada antes de la principal, con el mismo sujeto: primero acabaron, luego salieron.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase enfática.

items.texto: ___ was the noise, not the price, that worried her.

feedback.es: La frase enfática «It was… that…» destaca un elemento: aquí, el ruido y no el precio.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que mejor completa la frase.

items.texto: It was such a ___ memory that I could still smell the smoke.

feedback.es: «Vivid» es muy claro y detallado; «vague» y «weak» indican un recuerdo borroso, lo contrario de lo que dice la frase.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja con el contexto.

items.texto: The report does not prove it, but two workers ___ that the company hid the results.

feedback.es: «Allege» es afirmar algo sin pruebas; «deny» y «regret» no encajan con «does not prove it, but».

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo que mejor describe a la líder.

items.texto: A good leader is ___: she stays calm when a plan fails.

feedback.es: «Level-headed» es mantener la calma y pensar con claridad; «open-minded» es aceptar ideas ajenas.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa la frase.

items.texto: Constant rewards can ___ a change in our habits.

feedback.es: «Bring about» significa provocar o causar un cambio; «bring up» es mencionar o criar y «bring back» es devolver.

consigna.es: Dile con tacto a un amigo que debió avisarte: ya compraste la cena. Propón otro día.

items.respuesta: I was wondering if we could talk about dinner. You should have told me earlier, because I had already bought the food. Could we have dinner on Saturday instead?
aceptadas: I'm sorry to say this, but you should have called me earlier because I had already bought the food. Would it be possible to meet on Saturday instead?

feedback.es: Se espera «should have + participio» para el reproche, el motivo, una propuesta cortés y algún matiz de tacto.

consigna.es: Cuenta un rumor sobre el cierre de un parque y da tu opinión con un motivo (2–3 frases).

items.respuesta: It is said that the council is going to close the park next year. Given that many families use it every day, I think this would be a mistake.
aceptadas: The council is said to be closing the park soon. Given that families use it every day, closing it would be a bad idea.

feedback.es: Se espera una estructura impersonal para el rumor, tu opinión y un motivo («given that», «because»…).

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué pasó en la inauguración del festival.

items.audio: She was to have sung at the opening, but she lost her voice the night before. Her friend Sara sang instead and, to everyone's surprise, she was to become a legend. By the end of the year, Sara had recorded her first song.
opciones: A friend took the place of the planned singer.
The singer refused to perform at such a small event.
The opening was moved to the end of the year.

feedback.es: «Was to have sung» indica un plan que no se cumplió: la cantante prevista perdió la voz y su amiga la sustituyó.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige por qué no llegaron a tiempo a la ceremonia.

items.audio: We set off in good time. But for the repairs on the bridge, we would have reached the hall before the ceremony began. As it was, we slipped in during the first speech, and nobody seemed to mind.
opciones: They set off later than they had planned.
Repairs on the road held them up.
The ceremony began earlier than announced.

feedback.es: «But for the repairs» equivale a «de no ser por las obras»: las obras los retrasaron, aunque salieron con tiempo.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué se sabe del alcalde.

items.audio: The mayor allegedly accepted gifts from a builder, but nobody has any proof so far. Personally, I think he is probably not to blame. In all likelihood, the council will call a meeting next week, although it may well wait for the police report.
opciones: He has admitted taking gifts from a builder.
The speaker is certain that he did nothing wrong.
He is accused of taking gifts, but nothing is proved.

feedback.es: «Allegedly» señala una acusación sin pruebas, y «probably» es cautela: quien habla no afirma que sea inocente.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué hace la persona ante la pregunta.

items.audio: Thank you for that question. Let me clarify what I meant: the plan is not free, but it is cheap, because volunteers will cover most of the work. I take your point about the cost, though, and I am willing to review the budget once we have the first results.
opciones: He says the question has nothing to do with the plan.
He explains his idea and accepts that the concern is fair.
He promises that the plan will cost nothing at all.

feedback.es: Aclara lo que quiso decir y con «I take your point» reconoce que la preocupación por el coste es razonable.

consigna.es: Lee el correo y elige qué tono usa Mia con el casero.

items.texto: Dear Mr Brown, I am writing to report that the boiler in flat 4 is leaking again. I called a plumber yesterday, but he cannot come until Friday, and the flat is very cold at night. I do not wish to complain, but this is the second leak this winter. I would be grateful if you could arrange a faster repair or, at least, send us a heater in the meantime. Thank you for your understanding. Yours sincerely, Mia
opciones: Polite, but firm about the problem
Kind, and sorry as if she were guilty
Angry, and ready to leave the flat

feedback.es: Usa fórmulas corteses («I do not wish to complain», «I would be grateful if») pero deja claro que es el segundo problema: cortés y firme.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige cuál es la postura de la autora sobre los uniformes.

items.texto: Some people say that school uniforms are a waste of money, and I admit that they have a point: a jacket costs far more than a T-shirt, and children grow quickly. Even so, to be honest, I would never ban them. Uniforms reduce the difference between rich and poor families, and mornings are calmer when nobody argues about what to wear. In view of this, the best solution is cheaper uniforms, not no uniforms at all.
opciones: She thinks uniforms should be banned.
She accepts some criticism but still supports uniforms.
She believes uniforms are cheap and never a problem.

feedback.es: Concede que el coste es un problema («they have a point») pero con «Even so» mantiene su apoyo y propone uniformes más baratos.

consigna.es: Lee el texto y elige por qué el alcalde dice «Mistakes were made».

items.texto: Visitors to the old market often ask why the building looks so old and damaged. The roof should have been inspected years ago, and the crack in the north wall could have been repaired before last winter. Instead, the money was spent on a new car park. The council did have the walls painted by local students, which looks lovely, but paint cannot fix the damage. Asked who was to blame, the mayor only said: «Mistakes were made.»
opciones: It blames the students who painted the walls.
It denies that anything was done badly.
It admits errors without naming anyone.

feedback.es: La pasiva sin agente («were made») permite admitir errores sin decir quién los cometió, por eso evita asumir responsabilidad.

consigna.es: Lee la actualización y elige por qué se menciona el retraso de las fotos.

items.texto: Hi all, here is a quick progress update. So far, I have completed the first two sections of the guide, and the project is on track overall, although we are slightly behind on the last section. The main obstacle has been a delay in the photos from the school. With a tight deadline, I do not think it is realistic to finish everything by Friday, so I would propose moving the deadline to Tuesday. Could you let me know by Thursday whether that works for everybody?
opciones: To justify a request for a later deadline
To complain that the school does not help
To warn that the project may be cancelled

feedback.es: Es el obstáculo principal y la razón con la que justifica pedir más plazo; el resto del proyecto va bien.

consigna.es: ¿Qué frase, por sí sola, indica que lo previsto no llegó a ocurrir?

items.texto: Ana's train was cancelled on Saturday, so she did not go to the wedding.
opciones: She was to have gone to the wedding.
She was to go to the wedding.
She had gone to the wedding.

feedback.es: «Was to have + participio» expresa un plan pasado que no se cumplió; «was to go» solo nombra el plan, sin decir si se llevó a cabo.

consigna.es: Elige la frase correcta (condicional sin «if»).

items.texto: The rain stopped the match, so it finished late.
opciones: Hadn't it been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.
Had not it been for the rain, the match would finish on time.
Had it not been for the rain, the match would have finished on time.

feedback.es: En la inversión formal se mueve «had» al principio y «not» va después del sujeto: «Had it not been for...».

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la opción correcta.

items.texto: We took a hundred photographs, a few of ___ I am going to share.

feedback.es: Tras «a few of» se usa «which» para unir las dos cláusulas; «them» dejaría dos oraciones pegadas por una coma.

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la expresión adecuada.

items.texto: The new stadium is ___ as big as the old one, so the fans are disappointed.

feedback.es: «Nowhere near as… as» marca una gran diferencia a la baja: el estadio es mucho más pequeño, por eso los hinchas se decepcionan.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que encaja en el mensaje.

items.texto: Stop being so ___; it's my private message!

feedback.es: «Nosy» describe a quien se mete en lo privado de otros; «thrifty» es ahorrador y «generous» no encaja con el reproche.

consigna.es: Elige el adverbio que encaja en la frase.

items.texto: The museum is ___ open until nine, but the door was locked.

feedback.es: «Supposedly» indica lo que se dice, y el contraste con la puerta cerrada muestra que puede no ser cierto; los otros dos no encajan con «but».

consigna.es: ¿Qué significa «throw in the towel» en esta frase?

items.texto: After ten failed tries, Ana was tired and decided to throw in the towel.

feedback.es: «Throw in the towel» es una expresión hecha que significa rendirse; por eso, tras diez intentos fallidos, deja de intentarlo.

consigna.es: Completa el mensaje con la palabra correcta.

items.texto: Tom will ___ the minutes to all attendees by Tuesday.

feedback.es: «Circulate» es enviar un documento a todos los destinatarios; «approve» o «cover» no encajan con «to all attendees».

consigna.es: Escribe a una tienda: tu pedido llegó roto; pide solución con cortesía y despídete.

items.respuesta: Dear Mr Lopez, I am writing to complain that the laptop I ordered last week arrived damaged. I would be grateful if you could send a replacement or refund me, because I need it for work. I look forward to hearing from you. Yours sincerely, Ana
aceptadas: Dear Ms Ortiz, I am writing to report that my order arrived broken. I would appreciate it if you could arrange a refund as soon as possible. Kind regards, Leo

feedback.es: Se espera un correo formal: «I am writing to» para abrir, una petición cortés con «I would be grateful if» y un cierre formal.

consigna.es: Un amigo propone una fiesta semanal. Discrepa con tacto y propón algo (3–4 frases).

items.respuesta: I can see why you like the idea, but I'm a bit worried about the noise. I'd have thought once a month would be fairer for everyone, wouldn't you agree? How about a quiet dinner on Fridays instead? That way we would all be happy.
aceptadas: I take your point that we need to have fun, but I am not sure a party every week is fair on the neighbours. What about a small party once a month? I think that would suit everyone.

feedback.es: Se espera discrepar con tacto («I can see why», «I'm a bit worried»), matizar la opinión y cerrar con una propuesta («How about...?»).

consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué quiere realmente Kim de Dan.

items.audio: Hi Dan, it's Kim. I don't suppose you'd have time to look over the client's proposal today? No pressure, of course. It's just that the meeting has been moved to tomorrow morning, and I'd rather not be changing things at the last minute.
opciones: She is saying he can look at the proposal whenever suits him.
She is politely asking him to check the proposal today.
She wants him to move the client meeting to tomorrow.

feedback.es: «I don't suppose you'd have time…?» es una petición muy suavizada; «no pressure» es cortesía, y la reunión de mañana muestra que lo necesita hoy.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué opina en realidad la jefa sobre el informe.

items.audio: So I asked my boss what she thought of my report. She smiled and said, 'Well, it's not bad... for a first draft.' Then she asked whether I'd had time to check the figures again, and went straight on to the next item on the agenda.
opciones: She is not satisfied and expects a better version.
She is pleased and only wants the figures checked again.
She is angry and says so openly.

feedback.es: «Not bad… for a first draft» suena amable, pero da a entender que aún no está bien; pedir revisar las cifras y pasar al siguiente punto lo confirma.

consigna.es: Escucha a la directora y elige qué le comunica a Sam.

items.audio: Thanks for coming in, Sam. As you know, we've been reviewing the department, and I'm afraid we'll be letting some people go at the end of the month. You're one of them, I'm sorry to say. Of course, we'll give you a good reference and help you find something else.
opciones: She is offering Sam a move to another department.
She is asking Sam to write a reference for a colleague.
She is telling Sam that his job is ending.

feedback.es: «Let people go» es un eufemismo de despedir; «you're one of them» y la ayuda para buscar otro trabajo lo confirman.

consigna.es: Escucha al orador y elige cuál es su postura sobre el plan.

items.audio: Granted, the new scheme has drawbacks, and I wouldn't deny that some drivers will be unhappy. That said, the evidence from other cities is strong, so on balance I'd argue we should try it for a year and then review the results.
opciones: He rejects the scheme because drivers will be unhappy.
He admits the drawbacks but supports a trial.
He wants to wait a year before forming an opinion.

feedback.es: Concede los inconvenientes («granted», «I wouldn't deny») y aun así apoya probarlo («that said», «on balance»).

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige qué quiere dar a entender Mara.

items.texto: Hi Jo, thanks for having the party on Saturday. It was certainly memorable. I found the kitchen at eight on Sunday morning and, well, let's just say the floor needed some attention. I'm sure you all had a lot of fun, and I wouldn't dream of complaining. It might be nice, though, if next time a few of your guests stayed somewhere other than the sofa, the bath and the garden. Anyway, the cleaning products are under the sink. Also, the neighbours came by on Sunday to say hello, and they seemed quite surprised by the music. Cheers, Mara
opciones: She is annoyed about the mess and hints that Jo should clean up.
She enjoyed the party and would like Jo to organise another one.
She wants Jo to ask his guests to leave earlier next time.

feedback.es: Dice que no se quejaría, pero sus ironías («certainly memorable», «needed some attention») muestran que le molestó el desorden.

consigna.es: Lee la noticia y elige qué se puede concluir del dato sobre los beneficios.

items.texto: Commuters were left angry yesterday as the train company announced a fare hike of six per cent. A spokesperson insisted the increase was necessary to fund improvements, although critics claim that services have barely improved in years. According to a source close to the company, record profits were made last year, but when asked about this, the company declined to comment. The transport minister is expected to speak tomorrow, and a group of passengers has already asked for a meeting. Meanwhile, many say they will keep taking the train because they have no other choice.
opciones: It is true, because the company has not denied it at all.
It is not proven: one source says so and the company is silent.
It is false, because the company refused to talk about it.

feedback.es: Solo una fuente lo afirma y la empresa ni lo confirma ni lo niega («declined to comment»): callar no prueba que sea cierto ni falso.

consigna.es: Lee el fragmento y elige lo que muestra Anna frente a lo que siente.

items.texto: Anna answered every question in a level voice and smiled at the right moments. 'Of course,' she told Mr Hale, 'take all the time you need.' She had changed her answer six times in the taxi, but nobody would have known it. Only her hands, white around the pen, told a different story. Mr Hale glanced at them, then politely looked away and went back to reading. Everything depended on this meeting, and they both knew it. She moved in her chair, checked her watch, and waited, with the same polite smile, for him to turn the page.
opciones: She feels confident, and she shows it openly.
She is angry with Mr Hale for reading so slowly.
She looks calm, but she is very tense inside.

feedback.es: Su voz y su sonrisa parecen tranquilas, pero las manos tensas y los gestos nerviosos delatan lo que siente por dentro.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen y elige la conclusión más prudente.

items.texto: This study examined whether short daily reading sessions improve concentration. Sixty participants were randomly divided into two groups. One group read for twenty minutes a day for a month, while the control group did not. The reading group scored slightly higher on a concentration test. However, the sample was small and the difference was not large, so the results may indicate a benefit rather than prove one. Further research is needed to find out whether the effect lasts, and to check the results with a much larger and more varied group of people.
opciones: The study proves that reading helps, although the effect is small.
The study points to a possible benefit, but does not prove it.
The study found no real difference, so reading does not help.

feedback.es: La diferencia fue pequeña y la muestra limitada: solo se puede hablar de un posible beneficio; afirmar que está probado exagera y negar todo efecto ignora que el grupo puntuó algo más.

consigna.es: Elige la frase que dice que Leo actúa así ahora, aunque no sea su carácter.

items.texto: Everyone knows Leo as a patient, easy-going man, so his mood this week has surprised us.

feedback.es: «Is being + adjetivo» señala una conducta pasajera y fuera de lo normal; «is», «tends to be» y «by nature» describen el carácter o un hábito.

consigna.es: Completa con la coletilla con la que Leo muestra que no le cree.

items.texto: Mia: I repaired the car myself. Leo: Oh, you repaired it yourself, ___?

feedback.es: Una coletilla de la misma polaridad que la frase afirmativa («did you») suena a duda o burla; «didn't you» pediría confirmar un dato.

consigna.es: Completa la frase con la estructura formal de medio o consecuencia.

items.texto: The council has introduced a scheme ___ drivers pay a fee to enter the centre.

feedback.es: «Whereby» introduce una cláusula que explica cómo funciona un sistema («whereby drivers pay…»); los otros no se usan así.

consigna.es: Lee el titular y elige lo que significa.

items.texto: Council to close town pool after safety probe
opciones: The council is going to close the pool.
The council closed the pool a week ago.
The council has decided to keep the pool open.

feedback.es: En los titulares, «sujeto + to + verbo» anuncia algo previsto: el ayuntamiento cerrará la piscina, pero aún no ha ocurrido.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que completa el texto formal.

items.texto: Written down, all those reduced forms can ___ careless in a formal email.

feedback.es: «Come across as» significa dar la impresión de ser algo; las otras opciones no admiten un adjetivo a continuación.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo correcto para quien deduce algo.

items.texto: I ___ from his silence that he was unhappy, though he never said so.

feedback.es: «Infer» es deducir a partir de pistas; «imply» o «hint» los usa quien da a entender algo, no quien lo deduce.

consigna.es: Elige el adjetivo para una afirmación demasiado general y sin pruebas.

items.texto: The writer makes a ___ statement, 'everyone hates mornings', and offers no evidence.

feedback.es: «Sweeping» describe una afirmación demasiado amplia y sin pruebas, como «todo el mundo odia las mañanas».

consigna.es: Completa la expresión sobre mantener una postura bajo presión.

items.texto: When the manager pushed back, Lena refused to change her view and ___ her ground.

feedback.es: «Hold your ground» es mantener tu postura sin ceder ante la presión.

consigna.es: Un amigo propone un viaje caro. Recházalo con tacto en 3 o 4 frases y propón algo.

items.respuesta: Thanks for the idea, it sounds lovely. I'm afraid the budget is tight this month, so I'd rather not go. Perhaps we could spend a weekend in the city instead? I hope you don't mind.
aceptadas: Thank you for asking, it sounds great. I'm sorry, but I would rather not go because money is tight. How about a day at the beach instead? I hope that works for you.
That is very kind of you, but I am afraid I can't afford it this month. Would you be up for something cheaper, like a picnic by the river? I would still love to see you.

feedback.es: Agradece, rechaza con atenuadores («I'm afraid», «I'd rather not») y ofrece una alternativa concreta con «we could» o «how about».

consigna.es: Un compañero dice que todos deberían teletrabajar. Concede un punto y defiende tu postura.

items.respuesta: It is true that working from home saves time and money. Nevertheless, I still believe that the office is better for teamwork, because ideas spread faster when people meet. On balance, a few days at home seems the best solution.
aceptadas: I take your point that working from home is comfortable. However, I think the office is better for learning, and I wouldn't deny that some people work better alone. In my view, a mix of both works best.

Granted, remote work saves commuting time. That said, the office is better for teamwork, because ideas spread faster when people meet, so I would argue that everyone should come in at least twice a week.

feedback.es: Concede un punto con «it is true» o «I take your point», contrasta con «however» o «that said» y defiende tu postura con «I believe» o «I would argue».

consigna.es: Escucha y elige qué deduce la persona sobre el hombre de la feria.

items.audio: I spoke to a man at the book fair for about ten minutes. He didn't seem nervous at all, but every time I asked him something, he gave me a one-word answer and glanced at his phone. When I mentioned the new exhibition, he said, "Sounds interesting," and that was it. I got the impression he would rather have been somewhere else.
opciones: He was too shy to say much.
He was keen to hear more about the exhibition.
He wanted the conversation to be over.

feedback.es: No parecía nervioso, contestaba con monosílabos, miraba el celular y no mostró interés real: lo que se deduce es que prefería estar en otro sitio.

consigna.es: Escucha el parte y elige el consejo principal para los excursionistas.

items.audio: Conditions on the ridge are expected to deteriorate by mid-afternoon, with gusts of up to sixty kilometres an hour and poor visibility. Thunderstorms are possible, though not certain. Anyone who hasn't reached the summit by noon had better turn back, and people caught in the open should take shelter below the ridge.
opciones: Carry on as planned, since the weather will stay fine all day.
Wait on the ridge until the storms have passed.
Head down unless they are close to the top by midday.

feedback.es: El parte dice que quien no haya llegado a la cima a mediodía haría mejor en volver; además, si hay tormenta hay que refugiarse por debajo de la cresta, no en ella.

consigna.es: Escucha y elige la condición que pone la inquilina.

items.audio: I told the landlord I'd sign for two years on the understanding that he repairs the heating before winter. He said he'd consider it, provided I paid the deposit first. I've agreed to that, but only if the repair is written into the contract. Otherwise, I'm not budging.
opciones: She will pay the deposit only if the repair is put in writing.
She will pay the deposit only once the heating has been fixed.
She will sign for two years only if the landlord lowers the deposit.

feedback.es: Acepta pagar el depósito primero, como pide el casero, pero solo si la reparación queda escrita en el contrato; no espera a que arreglen la calefacción ni negocia el depósito.

consigna.es: Escucha y decide qué concluye la persona de la respuesta de su jefa.

items.audio: When I asked my manager whether I could work from home on Fridays, she said, "That might be difficult at the moment, but I'll think about it." I've worked there long enough to know how a polite "I'll think about it" usually turns out. So I didn't push, and I haven't mentioned it since.
opciones: The manager needs a few days to make up her mind.
The request will probably not be granted.
The manager is in favour of the idea.

feedback.es: Por la cortesía indirecta («might be difficult», «I'll think about it») y por su experiencia en esa oficina, deduce que la respuesta equivale a un no.

consigna.es: Lee el mensaje y elige por qué Leo escribe «don't feel any pressure».

items.texto:
Hi Marta,
It was lovely meeting you at the book fair on Saturday. I'd really like to pick up where we left off on translation, since I've been thinking about your point regarding jargon. I'm free on Thursday evening if you fancy a coffee, but please don't feel any pressure: I realise your week may already be full. Either way, I'll send you the article I mentioned, and perhaps we could take it from there. I also enjoyed hearing about your work, and I think we have a lot in common. Hope to touch base again soon!
Best, Leo
opciones: To warn Marta that the plan for coffee may well be cancelled
To make it easy for Marta to say no without feeling awkward
To hint that Leo himself may not be free on Thursday evening

feedback.es: La frase le da a Marta una salida fácil: puede declinar sin incomodidad, porque Leo reconoce que quizá tenga la semana llena.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen del informe y elige qué postura mantienen los autores.

items.texto: Sleep and screen habits: summary of findings. A survey of 240 students in two local schools, carried out last March, found that those who used phones after ten at night reported feeling more tired at school. It appears that late screen use may contribute to poorer sleep, although there is no conclusive evidence that it is the cause. Other factors, such as homework load or early starts, were not measured. To a certain extent, then, the results only hint at a link rather than prove one, and the authors recommend a larger study before any school policy is changed.
opciones: Late phone use is probably the main cause, although this is not yet proven.
Late phone use may play a part, but the survey cannot prove it.
Other factors, such as homework, probably explain the tiredness better.

feedback.es: Usan cautela («it appears», «may contribute», «no conclusive evidence»): el móvil puede influir, pero no se prueba que sea la causa principal y otros factores ni se midieron.

consigna.es: Lee la carta al periódico y elige qué sugiere la autora sobre la medida.

items.texto: To the Editor: The council's decision to ban cycling on the riverside path was, I assume, well meant. It is hard, however, to see whom it serves. Nobody I know has ever felt unsafe there, and in five years the path has seen one minor incident. Since the ban, cyclists have simply moved onto the main road, which is much busier. Pedestrians report no real difference, and the path itself is now rather quiet. Nobody was consulted, and the council has yet to explain its reasoning. I do hope someone will think again before anyone comes to harm.
opciones: It was a sensible step that needs more time to show results.
It helps pedestrians, although cyclists have reason to be annoyed.
It does little good and may even make things less safe.

feedback.es: Concede que tal vez fue bienintencionada, pero señala que nadie gana (los peatones no notan cambio) y que los ciclistas ahora van por una calzada más peligrosa.

consigna.es: Lee el artículo y elige qué da por supuesto el argumento que critica la autora.

items.texto: Some commentators argue that remote work has made teams lazy. Admittedly, a few companies have reported slower decisions, and that deserves a closer look. Nobody denies that some managers struggle to lead from a distance. Yet the argument treats the hours people spend at a desk as if they measured effort, which is hard to defend. Most of the evidence we have so far, albeit limited, points the other way: work has held steady, and staff are more willing to volunteer for extra tasks. The question worth asking, then, is not where people work, but how we measure what they deliver.
opciones: That remote work saves companies money
That teams decide faster when they meet in person
That time spent at a desk shows how hard someone works

feedback.es: El argumento criticado equipara las horas en la oficina con el esfuerzo («as if they measured effort... hard to defend»); por eso la autora propone medir lo que se entrega.

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre el servicio del transbordador.

items.texto: In the unlikely event ___ the ferry is cancelled, all passengers will receive a full refund.

feedback.es: Tras «in the unlikely event» se usa «of» + sustantivo («of a cancellation») o «that» + oración completa: aquí sigue una oración, así que va «that».

consigna.es: Completa la disculpa con la forma verbal que encaja.

items.texto: I'm sorry. Had I listened sooner, you ___ so alone now.

feedback.es: Es un condicional mixto: la condición es pasada («Had I listened») y el resultado es presente («now»), así que va «would not feel».

consigna.es: Completa la frase sobre la jornada de limpieza.

items.texto: Never before ___ so many neighbours joined the clean-up, and it is only ten o'clock.

feedback.es: Tras «Never before» se invierte el orden (auxiliar + sujeto); como el hecho llega hasta el presente, va el presente perfecto con sujeto plural: «have so many neighbours joined».

consigna.es: Elige la preposición que completa la frase.

items.texto: Owing to a shortfall ___ ticket sales, the club cancelled the final match.

feedback.es: El sustantivo «shortfall» se construye con «in» cuando nombra aquello que se queda corto: «a shortfall in ticket sales».

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que encaja en el mensaje de seguimiento.

items.texto: She hadn't replied to my message, so I sent her a gentle ___ to remind her.

feedback.es: «Nudge» es un empujoncito: un recordatorio suave para alguien que no ha respondido.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja en la entrevista.

items.texto: When the panel began to ___ into my reasons for leaving, I realised they wanted more than a short answer.

feedback.es: «Delve into» es profundizar con detalle en algo; «dodge» es esquivar y «deliver» es entregar, y ninguno encaja con «into my reasons».

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que encaja en la negociación.

items.texto: Both sides were firm, and neither would ___ a single point, so the talks ended without a deal.

feedback.es: «Concede a point» es admitir que el otro tiene razón en algo; «reciprocate» es devolver un gesto y «evacuate» es desalojar.

consigna.es: Elige la expresión que marca el límite de lo que aceptas.

items.texto: I'm happy to help with the garden, but I ___ at working every weekend.

feedback.es: «Draw the line at» es fijar un límite: ayudar sí, pero no trabajar todos los fines de semana.

consigna.es: Pide a tu jefa cambiar tu turno del viernes: sé cortés, da un motivo y ofrece otro día.

items.respuesta: I was wondering whether it would be possible to swap my Friday shift with someone else's. I have a medical appointment that I cannot rearrange, and I would be happy to cover a Saturday instead. Please let me know if that would be convenient.
aceptadas: Would it be possible to change my shift on Friday? I have a dentist appointment, so I cannot work that day. I could work on Saturday instead, if that would suit you.

feedback.es: Un registro formal suaviza la petición («I was wondering whether...») y ofrece una alternativa concreta.

consigna.es: Rechaza con tacto pasar la reunión al jueves: valora la idea y propón el lunes.

items.respuesta: That's a fair point, and I appreciate the suggestion. Although I see why you want to move the meeting, I'm afraid Thursday is difficult for me. Would it be possible to meet on Monday instead, provided that everyone is free?
aceptadas: Thank you for the idea, and I can see why Thursday suits you. However, it might be difficult for me that day. Could we perhaps meet on Monday instead?

feedback.es: Reconoce lo válido, matiza el rechazo («I'm afraid», «might be difficult») y ofrece una alternativa concreta.

consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje. ¿Qué piensa el hablante de la noticia?

items.audio: Guess what, the woman next door, she's only gone and landed a promotion! Honestly, I'd never have guessed, because she always seemed so noncommittal in meetings. Mind you, she does bend over backwards for everyone, so fair enough. Anyway, I think we should get her a card.
opciones: It is a surprise, but she deserves it.
She should not have got it, as she hardly speaks in meetings.
It is hard to believe, so somebody should check first.

feedback.es: La noticia le sorprende, pero con «mind you… fair enough» admite que ella hace más que los demás y lo merece.

consigna.es: Escucha. ¿Qué quería decir la hermana con su comentario?

items.audio: When I told my sister I had been picked to organise the whole party, she said, “Oh, what a relaxing weekend that will be.” I have had the guest list, the budget and the food to sort out since March. Then she laughed, and offered to bring the cake. Fair point, I suppose.
opciones: That the weekend will be a good rest for the speaker.
That organising the party will be hard work.
That the speaker should refuse to organise it.

feedback.es: Decir «qué fin de semana tan relajante» cuando hay lista de invitados, presupuesto y comida por resolver es sarcasmo: quiere decir que será agotador.

consigna.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz. ¿Cuál es la postura de Mia sobre el piso?

items.audio: Hi, it's Mia. Thanks for showing us the flat yesterday. It is lovely, honestly, and I suppose it could work for us. It is a bit pricey, though, so we would rather not commit at this stage. Could you hold it for us until we have checked the budget? I will get back to you by Friday.
opciones: She has turned it down and is being polite about it.
She likes it so much that she will take it.
She is interested but is not ready to decide yet.

feedback.es: Dice que es precioso y que podría servirles, pero el precio le frena y pide que se lo reserven hasta decidir: está interesada, sin decidir aún.

consigna.es: Escucha. ¿Qué está haciendo el hablante en este momento?

items.audio: Thank you, all three of you. Let me recap, because I think we agree more than it seems. Two of you find the plan tempting, but nobody is sure the budget will hold. Having said that, I am hearing that you would back it if there were a safeguard. Moving on, then: should the fee rise if demand falls? Who would like to start?
opciones: Criticising the plan because it lacks a budget
Summarising what was said and moving the panel on
Closing the debate because nobody can agree

feedback.es: Recapitula lo dicho («let me recap», «I am hearing that») y cierra con «moving on»: resume las posturas y reconduce el debate.

consigna.es: Lee el correo. ¿Por qué dejó el tema la madre anfitriona?

items.texto: Hi Jo, a small misunderstanding at dinner last night. My host mother asked whether I wanted to join her at the market on Saturday, and I said, “We will see,” because I was keen but unsure about my plans. She smiled, said, “Of course,” and quickly changed the subject, so I thought nothing more of it at the time. Afterwards my host brother explained that in their family “We will see” is a gentle way of saying no. Honestly, I felt embarrassed, because I do want to go. I am going to text her this morning, and I can hardly blame her for not asking twice. Mia
opciones: She took Mia's answer as a polite refusal.
She was offended by something Mia said at dinner.
She had already found somebody else to go with.
She forgot that she had invited Mia.

feedback.es: El hermano explica que «We will see» es una forma suave de decir no; por eso ella entendió un rechazo cortés y no insistió.

consigna.es: Lee el comunicado. ¿Cuál es la postura real de la asociación?

items.texto: Dear resident, the association has taken note of your complaint about the shared garden and regrets any inconvenience. We had a frank exchange of views at Tuesday's meeting, and we remain committed to keeping the space clean for everyone. At this stage, however, we are not in a position to promise a date for the work, and we would ask you to bear in mind that the budget has been tight all year. We will get back to you once the committee has reconsidered the matter, and we hope that the garden can then be enjoyed by all residents again. Yours sincerely, the Residents' Association
opciones: It has agreed to clean the garden by next week.
It understands the complaint but offers no guarantee.
It believes the complaint was unfair to the committee.

feedback.es: «Take note», «frank exchange of views», «not in a position to promise» y «reconsidered» son fórmulas corteses: reconocen la queja sin garantizar nada.

consigna.es: Lee el relato. ¿Qué debe sospechar el lector?

items.texto: I want to be clear about last Friday. I stayed in all evening, reading by the window, and I heard nothing unusual, not even the dog next door. My brother says he saw me near the harbour at ten, but he has always exaggerated, and he has never let me forget the business with the boat. The police officer asked about my boots, which were by the door, still wet. I told him it had rained earlier, which was true, although I did not mention that it had stopped by six. Naturally, I was home all night. Ask anyone you like, and you will find that my version of events has never changed.
opciones: That the brother is inventing a story to cause trouble
That the police officer has confused the narrator with someone else
That the narrator was out that night and is hiding it

feedback.es: Las botas mojadas y que la lluvia había parado a las seis contradicen su versión: es un narrador poco fiable que oculta haber salido.

consigna.es: Lee el resumen. ¿Cómo valoran los autores su propio resultado?

items.texto: A new survey of 300 teenagers suggests that those who sleep longer tend to score higher in exams. The authors, however, stop short of claiming a causal link. Only one school took part, and the sleep hours were self-reported, so some pupils may have exaggerated. The pupils were also all the same age, which limits how far the findings apply to other teenagers. Nor can the team rule out that confident, well-organised pupils simply sleep better and also study better. In their view, the finding is worth following up carefully with a larger and more varied sample, but it is too early to advise parents using these figures alone.
opciones: As strong evidence that sleeping longer improves marks
As an encouraging result that still cannot show a cause
As proof that confident pupils, not sleep, explain the marks
As too weak to be worth following up

feedback.es: Dicen que solo sugiere una relación, no descartan otras explicaciones y piden una muestra mayor: es alentador, pero no prueba una causa.

consigna.es: Completa con el eco que muestra sorpresa.

items.texto: “Honestly, I'd turn down an offer that meant moving abroad.” “___? I'd accept it straight away.”

feedback.es: «I'd turn down» es «I would turn down» (tras «had» iría un participio). El eco repite el auxiliar y mantiene la polaridad: «Would you?».

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la concesiva.

items.texto: Strict ___ the new rules may seem, nobody can claim they were applied unfairly.

feedback.es: «Strict though the rules may seem» es la estructura adjetivo + though + sujeto + may. «However» va delante del adjetivo; despite y unless no encajan.

consigna.es: Completa la condicional con inversión.

items.texto: ___ demand fall, we will draw on the cash reserve to pay the rent.

feedback.es: «Should + sujeto + infinitivo» sustituye a «if» en condicionales formales de posibilidad remota: «Should demand fall…».

consigna.es: Completa con la inversión que exige «Not until».

items.texto: Not until the final slide ___ how much the speaker had left out.

feedback.es: Tras «Not until…» al inicio se invierte auxiliar y sujeto: «did the audience realise». Las demás mantienen el orden normal.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la expresión.

items.texto: I was about to pay when it ___ on me that my wallet was gone, and my face went hot.

feedback.es: «It dawned on me that…» significa «caí en la cuenta de que…»: la expresión fija usa dawn.

consigna.es: Elige la palabra que completa la frase.

items.texto: Saying that “all teenagers are lazy” is a sweeping ___: one exception is enough to make it fall apart.

feedback.es: Una «sweeping generalisation» es una afirmación demasiado amplia que una sola excepción desmiente.

consigna.es: Elige el verbo que completa la colocación.

items.texto: A flawed design can ___ doubt on every result that follows from it.

feedback.es: La colocación es «cast doubt on»: poner en duda. «Lend weight to» haría lo contrario, reforzaría.

consigna.es: Completa con la palabra que describe un vínculo engañoso.

items.texto: Ice cream sales and swimming accidents both rise in July, but the link is ___: hot weather drives both.

feedback.es: Si el calor explica ambas subidas, el vínculo no es causal: es «spurious», una correlación engañosa.

consigna.es: Rebate con tacto el cobro de entrada al parque (3-4 frases).

items.texto: Tu vecino propone cobrar entrada al parque del barrio. Reconoce su ambición, rebátelo con firmeza y sugiere otra opción.
items.respuesta: Much as I admire the ambition of the plan, I have reservations about the fee. It is by no means the fairest option for families with three children. What matters is that the park stays open to everyone. I would suggest a small donation instead.
aceptadas: However much I admire the idea, I am not convinced by the fee. Charging families would be far from fair. What matters is that the park remains free for everyone. I would suggest a small donation instead.

Much as I appreciate the effort, I cannot back the fee, which is by no means fair to large families. What matters is the cost, and it is families who would pay. I would propose a small donation instead.

feedback.es: Concede algo con «Much as I admire…», expresa reservas («I have reservations», «by no means»), menciona la tarifa y propone una alternativa.

consigna.es: Resume el estudio y sus límites para tu grupo (3-4 frases).

items.texto: Datos: 300 alumnos; quienes duermen más sacan mejores notas; participó un solo colegio; las horas de sueño las contaron ellos mismos.
items.respuesta: The study suggests that teenagers who sleep longer score higher in exams. However, the authors stop short of claiming a causal link. Only one school took part, and the sleep hours were self-reported, so the figures may be biased.
aceptadas: The survey suggests that pupils who sleep more get better marks, but the authors cannot rule out other factors. A single school took part, and the hours were self-reported, so the results may be biased. A causal link is not justified yet.

feedback.es: Usa un verbo cauteloso («suggests»), evita afirmar causa («stop short of a causal link») y cita una limitación concreta (un solo colegio, datos autoinformados).
